terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Majae: the 1st, 7th and 15th. Ovid derives the name from majōrēs, “the elders”, one of three explanations he gives (F. 5.73, 427): partly right, since de Vaan (359, s.v. magnus) puts Majus with magnus and major.

phrases.latin: mēnsis erat Majus, majōrum nōmine dictus
phrases.english: it was the month of May, named after the elders
On the fifth of May (the modern way).

majus.claim: consonantal i written j, with no macron before it
majus.html: The vowel before intervocalic j is short and the syllable heavy, as in major.
